Theme

Latin word

gēns

gēns, gentis f.

noun, third declension; its genitive plural gentium serves for “international”

a nation, a people; in the genitive plural, of the nations: international; race, people, nation

In this lexicon

  • international

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Off. 3.69: aliud jūs gentium, aliud jūs cīvīle; Traupman 187: jūs gentium, international law; M-O s.v. international law

  • race

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Off. 1.53: ejusdem gentis, nātiōnis, linguae (Lewis & Short); Traupman 205

Examples

  • Itaque majōrēs aliud jūs gentium, aliud jūs cīvīle esse voluērunt

    So our ancestors held the law of nations to be one thing and the law of our own state anotherCic. Off. 3.69

    In the entry for international

  • propior est ejusdem gentis, nātiōnis, linguae, quā maximē hominēs conjunguntur

    closer is the bond of the same race, nation and language, by which people are most closely joinedCic. Off. 1.53 (Lewis & Short)

    In the entry for race
